title: Diffusion-DRF: Free, Rich, and Differentiable Reward for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
claim: Compared with scalar or yes/no feedback, rich structured feedback gives gradients that are more coherent and concentrated on prompt-violating regions.
layout: 4 rows by 5 frames, top-to-bottom; red circles mark the violation, heatmaps overlaid
description: A grid of four rows and five columns of video frames showing a baseball player in a white and blue uniform with the number 6. The top row, labeled Video Input, shows the raw frames. Red circles mark the jersey number, which conflicts with the prompt's 'number 66', shown in red italics in the caption beneath the grid. The next three rows are labeled VideoAlign, Vanilla-DRF and Diffusion-DRF. Each overlays a gradient heatmap on the same frames, with warm colors for high gradient magnitude. VideoAlign's heat is scattered at the frame edges and the lower background. Vanilla-DRF's is diffuse over the body and background. Diffusion-DRF's is concentrated on the number region. The eye goes first to the red-orange blobs in the heatmap rows.
caption: Gradient Analysis. In contrast to the latest scalar-based VideoAlign [ref] and our Vanilla-DRF baseline built on a simple yes/no text-video alignment VLM feedback, our Diffusion-DRF leverages free and rich structured feedback to empirically yield more semantically coherent and spatially concentrated gradients, with heatmaps that better align with regions where the generated video appears to violate the input prompt. We present more visualizations in [ref].
abstract: Video diffusion alignment has been heavily relied on scalar rewards. These rewards are typically derived from learned reward models in human preference datasets, requiring additional training and extensive collection. Moreover, scalar rewards provide coarse, global supervision, offering limited prompt-generation mismatch credit assignment and making models prone to reward exploitation and unstable optimization. We propose Diffusion-DRF, a free, rich, and differentiable reward framework for video diffusion fine-tuning. Diffusion-DRF employs a frozen, off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) as the critic, eliminating the need for reward model training. Instead of relying on a single scalar reward, it decomposes each user prompt into multi-dimensional questions with freeform dense VQA explanation queries, yielding information-rich feedback. By direct differentiable optimization over this rich feedback, Diffusion-DRF achieves stable reward-based tuning without preference datasets collection. Diffusion-DRF achieves significant gains both quantitatively and qualitatively, outperforming state-of-the-art Flow-GRPO by 4.74% in overall performance on unseen VBench-2.0.
